question: Keď bača na salaši vyrobí syr na bryndzu, zostane mu ovčia srvátka. Pod akým menom ju poznáme z reštaurácií, kde sa pije k bryndzovým haluškám?
source_excerpt: A byproduct of the production of bryndza is Žinčica.

extra.why_interesting: Every Slovak has drunk or seen žinčica next to halušky, but few think of it as the leftover from cheesemaking. The 'aha' is linking a familiar drink to the bryndza process.
extra.verification_notes: Žinčica is the Slovak beverage made from sheep whey, a by-product of bryndza/sheep cheese production, traditionally served with bryndzové halušky (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%BDin%C4%8Dica).

explanation: Žinčica je vlastne odpad z výroby syra. Pastieri ju na salaši pili namiesto vody a vďaka mliečnym baktériám chutí jemne kyslasto.

question: Aby sa ovčie mlieko na salaši zmenilo na syr, z ktorého bude bryndza, musí ho bača zraziť syridlom. Z ktorej časti tela zvieraťa sa syridlo tradične získavalo?
source_excerpt: Rennet is a complex set of enzymes produced in the stomachs of ruminant mammals.

extra.why_interesting: Players picture bryndza as just milk, salt and a shepherd's patience, and assume the milk curdles on its own or with some herb. The answer is that the key ingredient comes from a young animal's stomach, which is surprising. Players can still reason toward it: milk has to curdle somewhere, and a suckling animal's stomach is where that naturally happens.
extra.verification_notes: Rennet is traditionally obtained from the lining of the abomasum (fourth stomach) of young ruminants, so 'zo žalúdka' is correct (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rennet); I did not open this page, so the verdict rests on general knowledge.

explanation: Syridlo sa tradične získavalo zo žalúdka mladých teliat alebo jahniat, ktoré ešte pijú len mlieko. Ich žalúdok obsahuje enzým, ktorý mlieko zrazí, takže hrudka na bryndzu vzniká vďaka tomu istému procesu, akým mláďa trávi mlieko.
